findings.title: State-dependent revision authority is a simple direct reduction baseline
findings.source: Zhao et al., When Tools Hurt LLM Reasoning: State-Dependent Belief Revision under External Evidence, arXiv:2508.15754; accepted EMNLP 2026
findings.external_fact: External evidence helps weak initial beliefs but can harm strong correct beliefs; CASE is a label-free certainty-based controller choosing whether to revise/use external evidence.
findings.implication: A positive Belief-R update/maintain result can reduce to revision-authority arbitration before persistent dynamics.

findings.title: Minimal-edit revision diagnostics separate update mechanisms
findings.external_fact: Support insertion, defeating-fact insertion, support removal, and irrelevant additions reveal distinct inertia/over-flip/abstention regimes not captured by static accuracy.
findings.implication: Any C19 follow-up should localize gain by edit class rather than rely on aggregate BREU alone.

findings.title: Transformer state tracking can implement an implicit finite-state automaton
findings.source: Zhang et al., Finite State Automata Inside Transformers with Chain-of-Thought, arXiv:2502.20129 (2025)
findings.external_fact: Mechanistic analysis identifies state-representing circuits consistent with an implicit FSA and tests skipped steps, noise and length generalization.
findings.implication: History-dependent state alone is reducible to ordinary finite-state computation; matched FSA/state-tracker baselines are required for stronger mechanism claims.

findings.title: State-space and transition complexity provide a controlled scaling discriminator
findings.source: Li et al., Scaling Laws for State Dynamics in Large Language Models, arXiv:2505.14892 (2025)
findings.external_fact: State-tracking accuracy degrades as state count grows and transitions become sparse across box tracking, DFA and text-game settings.
findings.implication: A future SparkBrain discriminator should compare error curves under controlled state-count, transition-density and horizon scaling rather than only fixed benchmark accuracy.

findings.title: Selective retention is an established alternative to persistent full-history dynamics
findings.source: Jiang et al., PABU: Progress-Aware Belief Update for Efficient LLM Agents, arXiv:2602.09138 (2026)
findings.external_fact: PABU explicitly predicts progress and selectively retains action-observation history, outperforming full-history baselines across AgentGym in the reported study.
findings.implication: Future long-horizon SparkBrain gains must distinguish persistent self-organized dynamics from compact selective-history belief state.
